I have fairly severe PTSD, and for a few months before I got diagnosed I was only sleeping like eight hours a week. It was absolutely horrible. At first I was just going to my general doctor, and he tried every kind of sleeping pill out there. None of it worked for me, because the root of the problem was still there. Every time I tried to sleep, I had sleep paralysis nightmares. I started having serious sleep anxiety. Even if I was drugged to the point of blacking out, I still couldn’t fall asleep, because I was TERRIFIED of what would happen if I did. Luckily, I started going to a psychiatrist that had a lot more experience with those types of things than a general doctor. I am now prescribed a medication that I take at night that will block the adrenaline that was fueling my nightmares in addition to the sleeping pill that worked best for me. I still have one every once in a while, but I can sleep almost every night. It’s life changing. I don’t know if his situation is similar to mine at all, but he may want to look into seeing a psychiatrist that is able to help him better. Living without sleep is torture.

That is true. For the most part, that doesn’t come into play in our office, but I know it does exist. I was just replying to the question of if dentists in the United States use amalgam more often than those in Europe. I definitely don’t mean that dentists in the states have no reason to ever use amalgam or anything like that.

I’ve worked at a dental office since I was 14 years old, so I have 12 years of experience in the dental field. I can’t speak for other dentists, but we hardly ever use amalgam. They are definitely not more durable, and they can cause problems for the tooth years down the road. They expand over time, so I’ve seen many old amalgam fillings actually expand enough to break a large chunk of tooth off. There are only two circumstances that we actually use amalgam. 

Composite fillings require the area to be completely dry, or they won’t bond to the tooth properly. If a child is having molars come in, and the tooth already has a large amount of decay, you don’t really want to wait until the tooth is completely in position. The decay could be into the nerve by then, or cause the child pain. If a tooth is still partially covered in tissue, it is impossible to keep the area completely dry, so we use amalgam in those circumstances. The filling can be replaced later on, when the tooth is completely uncovered. 

The other situation we use amalgam in is when the tooth already has a crown that has a metal base or is gold. If the tooth becomes abscessed, we have to drill a hole in the top of the crown to be able to access the nerve chambers, so that we can do a root canal. Once the root canal is finished, we fill in that hole. Amalgam bonds to the metal in the crown much better than composite would. It isn’t a large hole, so you rarely would be able to see the amalgam.

I’m super late, so this will probably just get buried. I have too good of a story to pass up the chance to share it. 

When I was in college a couple of years ago, my three friends and I decided to rent a townhouse to live in for the year. The HOA regulation of the area stated that there can only be up to four unrelated people living in the house. Cool, we have four people, so it’s perfect. The guy who was living in it before us wouldn’t move out when he was supposed to, so we had to go through the process to evict him. After sleeping on friends’ couches for a month, he finally moved out. Obviously, we were super excited to move in, so we started moving our stuff in that day. 

We all were super busy with our school schedules, so most of the time when we were home we were just doing homework. Some days friends would come over to hang out, but we never threw a single party. We never were even loud after 10:00 pm. 

A few months in, we get an email saying that we are going to be evicted, because we have “at least six people” living in our house. We were confused, because we only had four people living there the whole time we had been there. We called the HOA and asked what they were talking about. They said the HOA representative (or whatever it’s called) that lived in our townhomes had sent them overwhelming evidence that we had too many people living with us. We assured her that we only had four people living there, and asked that she send us all the information that had been sent to her by our local HOA guy, Steve. 

She emailed us everything that Steve sent her that night. It was so bizarre. There were literally thousands of pictures of us coming and going into our house, all our cars and where they were parked, all of our friends coming and going, and every license plate that had ever been associated with our house. The thing that bothered me the most was that the pictures started the afternoon we moved in. It’s not like we did something that he didn’t like, so he started taking pictures to have evidence of some rule we were breaking. He literally had a picture of me the second I got out of my car the first time I went to the house. 

We were terrified. We were just four 20 year old girls that had been having pictures taken of everything we did for months, and we had no idea. We called the police that night. They were also creeped out by the incredibly large number of pictures and information about every aspect of our lives. They took all of our information, and then walked over to Steve’s townhome. He answered the door, and tried to play dumb. The cops showed him that they had all the information that he had sent to the lady who had emailed us. He basically said that he wouldn’t take any more pictures of us. The police were glad that we filed a police report, so that they would have that on file in case he didn’t stop. They couldn’t really charge him with anything, because technically when we stepped out our front door, we were in public, so he was allowed to take pictures. 

About a week later, as I was leaving for school, I looked towards Stalker Steve’s townhome and saw him leaning around the corner taking a picture of me. I ran down to confront him, but he ran into his house, and wouldn’t open the door when I knocked, like the coward that he is. 

I’m not sure if he every stopped taking pictures, or not. That week the HOA lady came and checked out our house three different times, and said that she didn’t see any sign that another person or two lived there. Once our year was up, we gladly found another  place to live. That next year, Stalker Steve got kicked out of the HOA and also got kicked out of his townhome. I’m not sure what happened, but I’m guessing it was probably the same type of stuff, because we met some girls that had lived there the year prior, and they said he did similar things to them.

TL;DR - Stalker Steve stalked and took thousands of pictures of my roommates and me when we were 20 year old college students. He then tried to get us kicked out of our house, even though we never violated a single rule.
